payload.body: Tape delay is a human-made echo effect that records an audio signal onto a continuous magnetic tape loop driven by capstans, then reads it back from a playback head positioned a fixed distance downstream so the signal returns after a time set by tape speed and head spacing. Parameters: (1) delay time — set by tape speed and physical head spacing, typically 20 ms to 300 ms; (2) feedback — the amount of playback signal fed back to the record head, creating repeated echoes; (3) tape speed — determines playback pitch and noise floor; (4) head configuration — number and spacing of record/playback heads; (5) wow/flutter — mechanical instability of the tape transport affecting pitch stability. Mechanism of persistence: the effect persists as a physical apparatus — tape loop, capstan motor, record/playback heads, and preamp — and as a circuit topology emulated in digital plugins that model tape saturation, wow/flutter, and head spacing. payload.body: Gain is the measure of amplification factor — the ratio of an output signal magnitude to its corresponding input signal magnitude. Clipping is the waveform distortion that occurs when a signal's amplitude exceeds the maximum processing capacity of a system, causing the signal's peaks or troughs to be truncated at the system's amplitude ceiling. It manifests as hard clipping (abrupt truncation at the limit, producing odd-order harmonics) or soft clipping (gradual compression near the limit, preserving more waveform character). Clipping serves as both a design constraint (headroom management in amplifiers) and an effect (intentional overdrive in guitar amplifiers). It persists as a diagnostic concept and engineering parameter through measurement instruments (clipping meters, oscilloscope waveform inspection) and design specifications (maximum output level, headroom margins). payload.body: A comparator is a human-made electronic circuit or system that compares two input signals and produces an output indicating their relationship — typically whether one exceeds the other, whether they are equal, or which is larger. Parameters: (1) reference input — the signal or voltage to compare against; (2) signal input — the signal being evaluated; (3) hysteresis — optional positive feedback to prevent output chatter when inputs are near-equal; (4) output type — open-collector, push-pull, or digital logic compatible. Mechanism of persistence: it persists as physical integrated circuits (e.g., LM311, LM339), as functional blocks within audio processors and dynamics units, and as a design pattern in DSP implementations. In audio systems, comparators form the core of sidechain compression, limiting, gating, and companding — comparing an audio signal against a threshold or sidechain input to trigger gain reduction or mute. payload.body: A preamp is a human-made electronic circuit whose purpose is to increase the amplitude of a weak input signal to a line-level or suitable operating level for subsequent processing stages. Parameters: (1) input gain — the amplification factor applied to the input signal, typically adjustable from 0 dB to 60+ dB; (2) input impedance — the resistance presented to the source, matched to sensor/output characteristics (e.g., high-Z for guitars, low-Z for microphones); (3) output level — the nominal signal level delivered to the next stage; (4) noise figure — the amount of noise added by the preamp itself, critical for preserving signal quality at high gain settings; (5) phantom power — optional 48V DC supply for condenser microphones. Mechanism of persistence: it persists as physical circuit designs (discrete transistor, op-amp, or tube-based topologies), as integrated modules in mixing consoles and audio interfaces, and as standard circuit topologies documented in electronic engineering texts and taught in audio engineering curricula. [formal: preamplificatio | substrate: matter | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: A limiter is a human-made audio dynamics processor that automatically reduces gain when an input signal exceeds a set threshold, clamping the output to a maximum level to prevent overload or distortion. Parameters: (1) threshold — the signal level at which limiting begins, in dBFS or dBu; (2) attack time — the response time before limiting engages, typically 0–30 ms; (3) release time — how quickly limiting disengages after signal falls below threshold, typically 50 ms–2 s; (4) ratio — the compression ratio once threshold is exceeded, effectively infinite (∞:1) in hard limiting; (5) makeup gain — post-limiting amplification to restore perceived loudness. Mechanism of persistence: it persists as analog circuit topologies (VCA-based limiters, opto-limiters), as DSP algorithms in software plugins and hardware processors, and as a standard feature built into mixing consoles, digital audio workstations, and broadcast chain equipment. [formal: limitatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: A clipper is a human-made audio dynamics processor that limits signal peaks by truncating the waveform at a set threshold, producing characteristic flat-topped distortion and harmonic content. Parameters: (1) clip threshold — the amplitude level at which clipping begins; (2) clip shape — hard clipping with abrupt truncation or soft clipping with gradual rounding; (3) output gain — makeup gain applied after clipping to restore level; (4) bandwidth — frequency range to which clipping is applied, often full band or band-limited. Mechanism of persistence: it persists as analog hard-limiting circuits using diodes and comparators, as digital algorithms in audio plugins and hardware processors, and as a standard stage in broadcast and music production chains. [formal: clippatura | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.70]

Parameters: (1) sidechain source — the signal that triggers ducking; (2) threshold — level at which ducking engages; (3) ratio — amount of gain reduction applied; (4) attack/release times — speed of gain reduction and recovery; (5) depth — maximum attenuation. Mechanism of persistence: it persists as a DSP algorithm implemented in audio plugins, hardware processors, and broadcast mixers, and as a standard practice in music production and post-production for creating space for vocals over music. Parameters: (1) source input — the audio signal that triggers detection; (2) target input — the audio signal whose gain is controlled; (3) detector circuit — the envelope follower that converts source level to control voltage; (4) routing matrix — the patch configuration linking source to detector. Mechanism of persistence: it persists as a wiring convention in analog consoles, as a routing option in digital audio workstations and plugin sidechain inputs, and as a documented technique in audio engineering literature. [formal: sidecatena | substrate: behavior | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Not identity (Law 8c): sidechain is the routing mechanism; ducking adds the gain-reduction behavior and the purpose of making room for the foreground, so the routing is a functional principle ducking needs, not what ducking is. Parallel to the accepted compressor DEPENDS_ON threshold rung. Direction: ducking (dependent) -> sidechain (dependency).

A competent engineer calls a tape loop 'a delay' (the classic tape delay), so Law 9's competent-speaker test passes for the pinned sense ('a physical delay device'). Law 11e: delay-line exists as a sharper rung, but no accepted INSTANCE_OF chain yet connects tape-loop upward, so this first true connection is not derivable and the door does not refuse it — a leap is legal until the ladder exists. A competent speaker calls a de-esser 'a kind of compressor' / 'a special-purpose compressor'. This is the same specialization shape as the ALREADY ACCEPTED rung limiter INSTANCE_OF compressor ('a compressor with an effectively infinite ratio'); here the band-limited variant. Not identity (Law 8c): the de-esser is compressor PLUS band-limited detection — the specialization is what distinguishes the kind. Compressor is not reachable from de-esser over accepted INSTANCE_OF edges (de-esser's existing rung is audio-effect, a different branch), so the Law 11e door does not refuse. Direction: specific -> general.

Law 11: use is not kind. As sidechain's pending definition carves it — a ROUTING technique in which the control signal for a dynamics processor is derived from a different source — ducking is not a kind of routing. A competent speaker says 'ducking uses a sidechain' or 'sidechain ducking is a dynamics technique', not 'ducking is a kind of sidechain'. Law 9a's competent-speaker test fails for the pinned sense; the correct relation for what is actually claimed is DEPENDS_ON, which is filed separately (ge574de7edd2) and which I have advanced. Remove the band-pass-filter construct and the device is a generic full-band compressor, no longer a de-esser (the note's own conclusion). The BPF is a functional principle the de-esser needs to operate, not its identity (the de-esser is a dynamics processor, not a filter) and not its purpose — exactly the shape of the accepted wah-pedal DEPENDS_ON band-pass-filter rung I filed ('the band-pass filter is the functional principle the device needs'). Contrast my STRIKE of harmonic-exciter->filter: there the exciter's core operation (harmonic generation) proceeds without a filter; here the selective operation is impossible without band isolation. Pinned sense matches the target's accepted definition (passes a band, attenuates outside it). Direction: de-esser (dependent) -> band-pass-filter (dependency).

Law 8b removal test fails at the object level. The note pins the audio sense (soft clipping when signal exceeds a circuit's capacity) — a sense the web has accepted under saturation via its INSTANCE_OF rungs — but even on that pinning, gain is not what saturation operates by. Gain is the input/output RATIO: a description of the linear region and its departure. Remove the concept of gain and nothing stops saturating — the tape head still hits its flux ceiling, the diode still clips, the tank still fills, the market still saturates. 'Saturation IS the result of excessive gain' is constitutive assertion without a removal consequence (8b: constitutive ≠ dependency), and it misattributes the mechanism: you drive the INPUT past the limit, you do not 'drive gain' — gain is what gets reported as falling. replacementSpec.body: Amplification is the deliberate increase in the magnitude or intensity of a carried content, in two principal domains. (1) Physical: the increase in the amplitude or power of a signal by an active stage — parameters: an input signal, a gain factor (the ratio of output magnitude to input magnitude, reported linearly or in decibels), and a linear operating region bounded by a capacity limit beyond which the stage saturates; the mechanism is power conversion from a supply through active elements (valves, transistors, op-amps). (2) Rhetorical (auxesis): the strengthening of a claim or image by elaboration — parameters: a base claim, successive elaborations with repetition and intensification, and a cumulative effect that exceeds mere restatement. replacementSpec.body: Amplification is the deliberate increase in the magnitude or intensity of a carried content, in two principal domains. (1) Physical: the increase in the amplitude or power of a signal by an active stage — parameters: an input signal, a gain factor (the ratio of output magnitude to input magnitude, reported linearly or in decibels), and a linear operating region bounded by a capacity limit beyond which the stage saturates; the mechanism is power conversion from a supply through active elements (valves, transistors, op-amps). (2) Rhetorical (auxesis): the strengthening of a claim or image by elaboration — parameters: a base claim, successive elaborations with repetition and intensification, and a cumulative effect that exceeds mere restatement. Persistence: the physical sense persists through circuit design standards, electronics and acoustics textbooks, and calibration practice; the rhetorical sense persists through rhetorical handbooks, the teaching of composition, and the literary tradition. payload.body: Parallel compression is a human-made audio mixing technique in which a signal is routed simultaneously through one or more compressor paths and an unprocessed (dry) path, and the resulting outputs are blended back together, so the treated signal combines the density and level consistency of the compressed path(s) with the transient detail of the dry path. Parameters: (1) split configuration — the number of parallel compressor paths and their settings (threshold, ratio, attack, release), typically two or more paths at different intensities; (2) blend ratio — the relative level of the dry signal and the compressed signal(s) at recombination; (3) target material — the source signal treated (vocal, drum, bass). Mechanism of persistence: the technique persists as a documented studio practice — the 'New York' or 'NYC' compression recipe — maintained through engineer training, session templates, and DAW/plugin presets that encode the split-and-blend routing. [formal: compressio parallela | substrate: behavior | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.03]

Law 11d: the entry's accepted definition carves limiting as a dynamics processor that reduces gain above a set threshold to CLAMP the output and PREVENT overload or distortion — its design purpose is the opposite of producing distortion. The note pins a 'hard limiting that clips signal peaks' sense, but that construct is already named in the graph as 'clipping' (hard clipping = abrupt truncation at the limit), so the pinned sense is a different construct than the entry's accepted carving. A limiter is not a specific kind of distortion: a competent audio speaker would call it a dynamics processor (a kind of compressor — infinite-ratio limiting), and distortion's accepted definition carves effects that ADD grit/warmth/aggression by driving circuits beyond their linear range. If the filer meant the clipping construct, the nearest rung is 'clipping', not 'distortion' — and the sense still wouldn't ride on 'limiting'. The claim as filed fails the kind test.

Law 11d, judged on the pinned sense ('amplifier as used in audio signal processing'): the entry's accepted definition carves an amplifier as increasing amplitude 'while attempting to preserve the original waveform's shape and information content' — transparency is its design purpose. The accepted audio-effect definition carves a technique or device that 'intentionally alters a sound signal to change its perceptual character.' An amplifier's intended modification is level only; it is defined by what it does NOT change. A competent audio speaker would not call an amplifier 'a kind of audio effect' — in every rack and DAW topology, gain stages sit in the level/power category, distinct from effects (distortion, modulation, time, dynamics). The note's 'deliberate sound modification' reads 'modifies the signal' broadly, but the entry's own carving pins the opposite: preservation. Fails the kind test; the nearest kind it belongs to is a signal-processing circuit/device, not an effect.

The note's premise is false. Standard overlap-save applies NO window function: it takes overlapping blocks of input, zero-pads each to the FFT length, multiplies by the filter's FFT, inverse-transforms, and DISCARDS the first M-1 corrupted samples of each block (the 'save' is precisely keeping only the valid samples). That discard mechanism is what makes windowing unnecessary — overlap-save is the standard windowing-FREE alternative to windowed FFT convolution. Removal test of Law 8: remove windowing from the world and overlap-save operates identically; nothing in its mechanism requires a window function. The note argues 'segments must be windowed before the FFT to reduce spectral leakage' — that is not overlap-save, that is a different (windowed) approach, so the note justifies a different pairing (Law 36-adjacent: the justification does not address the actual claim). No dependency; STRIKE.

The entry's accepted definition carves clipping as truncation of peaks 'at the system's amplitude ceiling' — and that ceiling is exactly what the threshold entry carves: 'a defined point of crossing that mediates between two states,' here the linear pass-through state and the truncated state. Law 8 removal test: remove the concept of a defined crossing point and the operation 'truncate at the ceiling' loses its defining parameter — a clipper with no level at which to clip is not a clipper; the phenomenon's operating point IS that threshold. Not identity (Law 8c): clipping is the waveform phenomenon, threshold is its operating level — the phenomenon is not the level, but it cannot operate without one. Not purpose: the threshold is not what clipping is FOR, it is where it operates. The note pins this sense and it rides on both accepted definitions. Same accepted shape as limiting→threshold (the operating level of the clipping family). ADVANCE.

Pinned sense judged against target's accepted def (Law 11d). Distortion's accepted carve: an audio effect produced by driving a signal beyond linear range, INTENTIONALLY generating new harmonic content (grit/warmth/aggression). Limiting's accepted carve: a dynamics processor that reduces gain above threshold, clamping output 'to prevent overload or distortion' — its defining function is the avoidance of distortion, not its production. The note's bridge is 'it produces distortion by truncating peaks' — but producing an effect as a byproduct of gain clamping is not being a kind of that effect (cf. accepted precedent: exciter is not distortion; purpose != grit). A limiter's operation is variable gain control; the flat-topped output is clipped, yes, but the limiter is not a clipping operation — 'clipper' sits on the distortion rung, 'limiter' sits on the DRC rung (accepted edge: limiting INSTANCE_OF DRC). Nearest kind (Law 11e) is DRC, already on the map; distortion is a sibling branch two rungs over. A competent engineer files limiters in dynamics, not in distortion effects. STRIKE on the pinned sense.

The pinned premise is false as a matter of the method's actual design. Overlap-save (FFT block convolution) takes input blocks of length L+N-1 (N = filter length), zero-pads to an FFT length, multiplies by the filter's FFT, inverse-FFTs, and DISCARDS the first N-1 samples of each output block — those are exactly the samples contaminated by circular convolution. The discard step, not a window, is what makes the result exact linear convolution. Overlap-save is the standard window-free block method; no window function appears in it at all. DEPENDS_ON test (Laws 2b/8b): remove windowing — does overlap-save stop operating? No: it operates exactly as designed without any window. 'Must be windowed to reduce spectral leakage' describes spectral-estimation practice (periodogram windowing), not the mechanics of block convolution. A dependency on a concept the method never uses cannot stand. STRIKE.

Pinned sense judged under the removal test (Laws 2b/8b). Clipping as an audio processing technique is threshold-gated by its own definition: a clipper passes the signal below a defined level and holds it flat above — output = clamp(x, -A, +A) — where A IS the threshold. Remove the concept of the defined crossing point and the operation has no boundary to truncate AT: no distinction between the passing region and the cut region, no flat-top, no 'clipping' as a named operation. Even in passive physical clipping (an op-amp at its rails, a vinyl groove at max depth) the rail/limit is precisely the crossing point that mediates between linear and truncated operation — the concept is constitutive, not incidental. Not purpose (8c): the threshold is not what clipping is for, it is the condition its operation runs on. Consistent with the accepted family on the map: limiter DEPENDS_ON threshold, compressor DEPENDS_ON threshold, noise-gate DEPENDS_ON threshold are all ACCEPTED — clipping (a clipper is a limiter at ∞:1) sits on the same rung. ADVANCE.
